records.finding: The em-dash fixture used \xHH printf escapes dash does not interpret; the newly wired CI step would fail deterministically on ubuntu-latest, blocking every PR — a local-green/CI-red skew in the very suite meant to kill one.
records.evidence: dash scripts/commit-lint-test.sh -> 'FAIL: hmb fixture is not 102 bytes', exit 1; bash passes.
records.reason: POSIX octal escapes in the printf format with %s for the filler; suite verified green under dash and bash separately (no || fallback masking).

records.finding: The 101-byte boundary case was shape-invalid ('xfeat:'), so it passed even with the byte cap deleted — the advertised boundary was unpinned on the fail side.
records.evidence: Examiner ran it against a cap-neutralized lint (-gt 100000): still rejected via the convention regex.
records.reason: Replaced with a shape-valid 101-byte header (with its own byte-count self-check) that fails only via the cap; examiner-proven to isolate the cap.
